As the US devotes significant resources to conflicts in the Middle East and efforts to counter China and Russia, its capacity to actively engage on the Korean Peninsula has diminished, some closer observers of North Korea say.

“North Korea is exploiting this period as a golden opportunity to accelerate the development of its military capabilities,” Lim said.

In 2024, United Nations experts said North Korea’s cyber thefts and illicit financial activities could be funding about 40% of its weapons of mass destruction programs. And every successful crypto heist adds to Kim’s ability to build out his army and threaten US ally South Korea, along with the 28,500 American troops stationed on the Korean peninsula.

Nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles have always been top priorities for the regime and its cash “but now there seems to be enough to support conventional forces, including new naval vessels, investments in drone tech,” said Adam Farrar, a former director on the US National Security Council covering Korea in both the Trump and Biden administrations.

North Korea might still be decades behind South Korea’s military in many ways, but maybe not for much longer, said Farrar, now a senior analyst at Bloomberg Economics.

title: Alphabet kicks off sale of its second euro bond this year
article:
(Nov 2): Alphabet Inc is offering euro bonds for the second time this year, in a test of investor demand after stress in technology debt pushed borrowing spreads wider across the sector in recent weeks.

The Google parent has opened the books on a seven-part sale spanning maturities from two to 19 years, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified. Initial price thoughts on the two-year fixed-rate tranche are around 60 basis points over mid-swaps while the 19-year notes are being offered at about 205 to 210 basis points over mid-swaps.

The deal comes after disappointing results from Alphabet last week intensified concerns over the scale of artificial-intelligence spending and helped drive spreads wider across technology debt. On Friday, contracts protecting against a default in Alphabet’s debt jumped 6.4 basis points, a record daily increase in absolute terms, to hit an all-time high of almost 91 basis points.

A day earlier, its stock had suffered its biggest daily drop on record after disappointing search and advertising sales, boosting fears that AI is a threat to its core business.

Technology companies are expected to continue borrowing heavily to fund AI investment, even as recent sales have faced weaker demand and wider pricing. Alphabet has maintained a capital-spending outlook of as much as US$205 billion for this year.

Alphabet raised €9 billion across six tranches in May. Barclays plc, BNP Paribas SA and Deutsche Bank AG are arranging Monday’s offering, which is expected to price later in the day.

title: BP gets US$6 bil to pay down debt as Castrol deal closes
article:
(Nov 2): BP plc completed a deal to offload its Castrol lubricants business, giving the oil and gas major US$6 billion to pay down debt as it works to repair the balance sheet.

BP agreed at the end of last year to sell a 65% stake in Castrol to US investment firm Stonepeak Partners, marking a key milestone in the company’s efforts to reset its business after years of underperformance.

The firm is channelling excess cash toward reducing financial obligations, which include conventional debt, hybrid bonds, leases and settlement payments for the Deepwater Horizon disaster. Net debt totalled US$13.87 billion at the end of the third quarter, BP said last week as it reported bumper earnings.

“This deal brings meaningful cash proceeds to BP today while retaining a valuable stake in Castrol’s future growth,” CEO Meg O’Neill said in a statement on Monday. “It will now have greater independence to accelerate its next phase of delivery.”

BP has completed a series of disposals as it attempts to simplify its business, focusing investment on its core upstream, downstream and trading operations. O’Neill, who in April became the first outsider to take the helm, is preparing to lay out her long-term strategy in December.

title: German firms Mahle, Schott said to seek banks for India IPOs
article:
(Nov 2): Two German companies, Mahle GmbH and Schott Pharma AG, are exploring initial public offerings of their Indian businesses that could raise as much as US$400 million each, according to people familiar with the matter, as multinational firms seek to tap the premium valuations commanded by their locally listed peers.

Schott Pharma executives met with investment banks last week for a potential IPO of Schott Pharma India pvt while auto-parts maker Mahle has invited banks to pitch for roles on a possible listing of its Indian operations this week, the people said, asking not to be identified because the discussions are private. Both Schott and Mahle are expected to appoint advisers soon, they said.

Deliberations are at an early stage and details including the size, structure and timing of the potential offerings could change, the people said. Representatives for Mahle and Schott Pharma did not respond to requests for comment.

India was the top global market for IPO fundraising last month, thanks to the blockbuster share sale of Jio Platforms Ltd, just as fundraising slows elsewhere with investors becoming more selective. IPOs have slowed to a near standstill even in the US, where the market is focused on the coming megadeal of Anthropic PBC. The Indian units of several global companies trade at significantly higher valuation multiples than their overseas parents, offering an opportunity to unlock value through local share sales.

Schaeffler India Ltd, for instance, trades at about 41 times trailing 12-month earnings, compared with 32 times for parent Schaeffler AG. Siemens Ltd, meanwhile, trades at about 62 times one-year forward earnings, compared with roughly 23 times for its German parent Siemens AG.

Schott Pharma India manufactures pharmaceutical glass packaging products for drugmakers and other healthcare customers, according to the company website.

See also: Jio shares indicated 22% higher in India grey-market trading

Mahle makes automotive products including filters, engine components and thermal-management systems, the company website showed. The company has 11 production locations and employed more than 4,600 people in India as of 2025, according to its annual report. India was the company’s fastest-growing region that year, with sales rising more than 10% to €455 million. On a currency-adjusted basis, revenue increased more than 20%.

title: Euronext joins industry push to integrate Nordic capital markets
article:
(Nov 2): Stock exchange operator Euronext NV has joined the Nordic Compass alliance, a consortium of three dozen of Northern Europe’s largest companies advocating for closer regional ties.

The addition of Euronext comes as Nordic Compass prepares to lay out its agenda at an inaugural summit this week, which is expected to include proposals to further integrate the region’s capital markets.

Spokespeople for both Euronext and Nordic Compass confirmed the company’s entry in response to Bloomberg News questions, with an official announcement planned later in the day.

The alliance is bringing together three rival financial market infrastructure operators, raising the prospect of more effective cross-border integration.

Paris-based Euronext, which runs the Oslo stock exchange along with post-trade infrastructure in Denmark and Norway, competes with Nasdaq Inc. for trading and listings and with Euroclear Holding NV for settling transactions and safekeeping securities.

Nasdaq is a founding member of Nordic Compass, while Euroclear joined the consortium in recent weeks.

See also: Brookfield taps KB Kookmin Bank to lead Korea’s first GPU loan at US$8 bil

Oslo Bors chief executive officer Øivind Amundsen said in September that he welcomed the Nordic Compass initiative but stopped short of saying Euronext would join.

The push, which has gained the backing of the likes of buyout group EQT AB and Nokia Oyj, comes as Nordic countries are seeing some of their most promising businesses seek financing or listings in the US or relocate altogether.

Swedish finance company Klarna Group Plc shunned Stockholm for New York for its initial public offering last year, while smart-ring maker Oura Inc, founded in Finland, attempted a US listing in September.

See also: PBOC conducts overnight reverse repo as policy anchor shifts

Capital markets are one of Nordic Compass’ four areas of focus, with increased cooperation in defence, deep-tech and energy also on the alliance’s priority list.

title: Ryanair initiates cost drive to offset US$2 bil fuel surge
article:
(Nov 2): Ryanair Holdings plc will embark on a cost purge across its airline to help offset a €2 billion increase in fuel charges next year, as the Middle East conflict continues to drive up oil prices and weighs on consumer willingness to book flights.

The airline will review airport deals, consider lowering crew staffing on planes and may increase the use of artificial intelligence to bring down expenses, it said Monday after reporting a 15% drop in profit after tax for the first fiscal half of the year.

“Everything is on the table, as we say, whether that’s pay freezes or other areas,” chief financial officer Neil Sorahan said in an interview. “I think we’re looking at a higher oil environment for possibly the next 12 months; we need to tighten our belt for the next 12 months.”

Fares in the first six months dropped as the US-Iran war triggered hesitancy among consumers and later bookings, Ryanair said. Jet fuel prices are expected to remain elevated next year, leading to significantly more expensive fares, it added.

Profit after tax for the period was €2.15 billion, down from €2.54 billion the year prior, Ryanair said. Unit costs rose 5%, unhedged fuel prices doubled to about US$130 a barrel and Ryanair no longer booked compensation for delayed aircraft deliveries.

The results come after Ryanair pared back its annual passenger target for this fiscal year and the airline said it plans to run a slimmed-down winter schedule to protect against rising oil prices. It now plans to fly 214 million passengers in fiscal year 2027, compared with the previous forecast of 216 million flyers.

See also: Thailand puts Bangkok on 24-hour flood watch for IMF meetings

For fiscal year 2028, Ryanair plans to grow traffic to more than 220 million passengers with the help of the new Boeing Co 737 Max 10s in its fleet in time for the summer season. The company said it will pay a dividend of €0.273 a share in late February 2027 and initiated another €800 million share buyback that will start that same month.

Ryanair, the largest low-cost carrier in Europe, is the first major European airline to report earnings for the quarter, setting the tone for the rest of the industry. US carriers such as Delta Air Lines Inc and American Airlines Group Inc have already cut their full-year outlooks, demonstrating how the sector is struggling to forecast results as fuel prices drive up expenses.

Shares of the Irish airline have fallen about 23% so far this year, compared with an 11% decline in the Bloomberg world airlines index. Ryanair’s decline is on par with rival Wizz Air Holdings plc. Another competitor, EasyJet plc, has increased 33% on the heels of its takeover agreement with Apollo Global Management Inc.

See also: World-first green flight levy in Singapore adds to rising costs of air travel

While Ryanair said it has zero visibility for the fourth quarter, demand for the third quarter is strong. Consumers tend to avoid long-haul flights and travel closer to home during a high-cost environment as they tighten their belts, Sorahan said.

title: Blackstone leads US$3.1 bil deal to acquire LNG Canada stake
article:
(Nov 2): A Blackstone Inc-led investor group agreed to acquire a stake in LNG Canada’s liquefaction business from a Mitsubishi Corp subsidiary for US$3.1 billion.

Other investors in the transaction for a 49.9% stake in LNG Canada’s business owned by the Mitsubishi unit include Canada Pension Plan Investment Board, Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System, the Investment Management Corp of Ontario and the Public Sector Pension Investment Board.

Mitsubishi, one of Japan’s largest liquefied natural gas suppliers, will remain the controlling partner and keep its full share of the LNG offtake, according to a statement Monday.

The choking of energy transportation through the Strait of Hormuz since the Iran War has spurred LNG importers to seek out supplies beyond the Middle East. Meanwhile Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has relaxed environmental restrictions and embraced conventional energy development more than his predecessor Justin Trudeau.

Shell Plc owns 40% in LNG Canada, the country’s first and only large-scale LNG export terminal, and Mitsubishi has a 15% stake. In September, investors led by Shell greenlit plans to double its export capacity to 28 million metric tons a year. Project partners have been looking to sell down their stakes in the project to fund the expansion.

Blackstone president Jon Gray called Canada a “sleeping giant economically” at an investment summit in Toronto in September. Canada’s natural resources, looser regulatory policies and access to private capital offered the country massive opportunities to grow, Gray said.

See also: Goldman hikes oil-price forecasts on ‘substantial’ supply risks

“This announcement builds on our deep conviction in Canada, our partnership with the country’s leading institutional investors and our ability to provide large corporates with flexible solutions to unlock value from their most critical assets,” Zachary Rubenstein, a managing director at Blackstone’s credit and insurance business, said in the statement.

Blackstone is providing the equity investment from its credit and insurance business. The nearly US$1.4 trillion asset manager refers to these types of deals as corporate solutions.

In August it announced a C$2.5 billion (US$1.8 billion) minority equity investment in Aeroplan Inc, Air Canada’s loyalty programme. Blackstone also led a US$5.34 billion investment in Williams Cos power plants alongside Apollo Global Management Inc and KKR & Co, and backed Rogers Communications Inc’s wireless network infrastructure with a C$7 billion deal last year.

title: Bitcoin’s resilience after Binance hack masks market jitters
article:
(Nov 2): Since the record cyber theft against the world’s largest crypto exchange last week, traders bracing for the worst have instead watched bitcoin pull off an unexpected feat: defying gravity.

The original cryptocurrency rose about 1% on Monday, trading around US$78,300 at 1pm in Singapore. It is down roughly 4% from Thursday’s high before Binance disclosed a hack that would ultimately see US$6.3 billion of user funds syphoned off. The token’s resilience has widely been attributed to the swift response from Binance, which promised from the start to cover all losses.

“Bitcoin holding up over the weekend is essentially a vote of confidence in Binance’s statements,” said Caroline Mauron, co-founder of Orbit Markets. “The market is clearly convinced that Binance has enough funds to cover the losses.”

Bitcoin was already under pressure last week from a selloff in risk assets, so its relative buoyancy underscores how differently traders are treating the incident than during the last major calamity to strike one of the largest crypto exchanges. During the 2022 collapse of the then second-largest exchange, FTX, bitcoin fell 19% over three days as the company run by former billionaire Sam Bankman-Fried went from a liquidity crunch to bankruptcy.

Sean McNulty, a derivatives trader at market maker AQC Tech, said one reason for bitcoin holding up better this time around is that Binance is buying the token to make users whole. But underlying sentiment remains uneasy, he said.

See also: Binance details US$3.6 bil in net outflows after cyber theft

“People see this as the tip of the iceberg and expect more hacks to happen given the AI capabilities,” said McNulty, referring to the use of artificial intelligence in cyberattacks this year. “If Binance, the world’s largest exchange, can be hacked, then no one is safe.”

In a sign of underlying nerves, there’s growing demand for near-term protection against a bitcoin decline. The one-day 25-delta put skew, a measure of how much more traders are paying to protect against a sizable drop than to bet on a comparable rise, climbed about 1 percentage point in 24 hours to 6.37 points, according to data based on options on crypto derivatives platform Deribit.

Kelly Ye, head of research at the trading firm Talos, said traders are responding differently to the hack compared with FTX’s collapse, which involved fraud.

See also: Binance in talks for Malaysian licence after five-year absence

“The market treated this as an operational shock, not a systemic one,” Ye said, noting that order book depth on Binance dropped 25% to 30% but that buyers returned within hours. “That’s a very different picture from 2022, when confidence drained out of the whole market.”

The greater near-term impact on crypto markets could come from the US midterm elections on Tuesday. A change in party control of Congress “could have meaningful implications for how crypto market structure legislation moves forward,” said Jeff Ko, chief analyst at ViaBTC.

Before last week, the largest crypto-related hack was in 2025 on the exchange Bybit, which lost roughly US$1.5 billion. The Federal Bureau of Investigation linked both the Binance and Bybit breaches to the North Korean hacking group TraderTraitor.

As with Binance, the Bybit hack initially had a relatively muted impact on bitcoin. Losses mounted in the days that followed, however, leaving the cryptocurrency about 14% lower a week after the Feb 21 attack.

With the latest hack, Ye said traders best positioned to identify the market disruption as it happened had spread their exposure across multiple exchanges.

“For institutions, the lesson is simple: no single venue is a safe place to hold risk or to read prices,” she said.

title: Taiwan said to ease exporter FX rule after record stocks exodus
article:
(Nov 2): Taiwan’s central bank is said to have eased restrictions on exporters selling US dollars to support the local currency after record foreign stock outflows helped make it Asia’s worst performer last month.

The Taiwan dollar rebounded from its weakest level since April 2025 on Monday after the central bank told some lenders that exporters’ US dollar sales would no longer face daily limits, according to foreign-exchange traders. The currency slid about 2% in the previous month amid persistent equity outflows.

The move was more pronounced in one-month non-deliverable forwards, which are used to hedge currency moves. The contracts strengthened from as much as 0.4% to 32.537 per US dollar after falling earlier.

“Given the underperformance of the Taiwan dollar, the headline is a signal that the authorities could be becoming less tolerant of Taiwan dollar depreciation,” said Eddie Cheung, senior emerging markets strategist at Credit Agricole CIB Hong Kong Branch.

Taiwan’s central bank called at least four banks Monday morning in a rare move, without specifying how long the measures will stay in place, said the traders who asked not to be named discussing private matters. The central bank sets different daily limits on exporters’ dollar sales. It previously said that, as a general rule, exporters may sell up to US$10 million per day.

See also: Smartphone apps bury the case for a pan-Asian currency

The central bank’s FX department didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.

title: Copper recovers as easing tech rout, lower oil calm growth fears
article:
(Nov 2): Copper rebounded from its lowest close in a week as a rout in technology stocks subsided and oil prices pulled back, easing fears around global growth.

The metal rose 0.5% to US$14,229.50 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange at 12.37pm Shanghai time, after sliding 1.4% on Friday to close out a third weekly decline.

Most Asian stocks rose along with US equity futures as investors rediscovered their risk appetite on Monday while crude oil fell on a report that US President Donald Trump will give diplomacy more time before deciding whether to renew strikes against Iran after Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Copper has traded in a relatively narrow range near US$14,500 in the past two months, with investors tracking uncertainties on a number of fronts, including the sustainability of artificial intelligence spending, the prospects of US import tariffs on refined copper and the risk of military escalation in the Middle East.

The metal is also finding some support from growing signs of supply constraints at mines. Chile’s output sank to its lowest for at least two decades in the last quarter and the country is forecasting only a modest recovery next year.

Copper has a structural supply challenge that “keeps price risk firmly skewed to the upside as long as global growth remains resilient”, Jefferies Financial Group analysts wrote in a note.

See also: Hazy outlook for palm oil stocks: OCBC Group Research

Other metals were mixed, with aluminium down 0.5%, zinc flat and nickel up 1.3%.

title: Thailand eyes expanding its largest port to meet trade boom
article:
(Nov 2): Thailand’s Port Authority is exploring a further expansion of Laem Chabang port, the nation’s biggest deep-sea gateway, to handle increasing trade of products from automobiles to electronics and petrochemicals.

“We’re already handling cargo volumes that exceed the port’s capacity and we’ve received complaints about congestion and delays in moving goods,” Decha Peukpattanaruk, chairman of Port Authority of Thailand, said in an interview. “We need to plan for further expansion as we expect cargo volumes to increase significantly in the coming years.”

The state agency is studying a potential fourth phase of development at the Chon Buri province port to add yet more capacity beyond an ongoing third-phase expansion, he said. The agency is assessing the potential future size of the port, investment requirements and a timeline, he said.

The port, about 120km southeast of Bangkok, is a key harbour for cargo ships transporting manufactured goods from Thailand’s industrial heartland. It is a centrepiece of the Eastern Economic Corridor, where Thailand has attracted investment in industries including electric vehicles, electronics, data centres and other advanced manufacturing.

The Southeast Asian nation’s exports and imports rose more than expected in September, propelled by global demand for electronic components and machinery tied to artificial intelligence and data centres.

See also: Saudi tanker giant posts 10-fold profit jump as ship rates surge

In the fiscal year ended September 2025, cargo volume at Laem Chabang jumped to a record of 10.2 million twenty-foot equivalent units of containers from 9.5 million units a year earlier, according to the agency’s data. In the first eight months through May 2026, the port handled 7.2 million units, the data showed.

The Port Authority plans to invite bids for new operators of the first and second phases of Laem Chabang after previous concessions expired several years ago, Decha said. Existing operators, including Hong Kong-based CK Hutchison Holdings Ltd, the port’s largest cargo handler, have been allowed to continue operating the facilities on a temporary basis, he said.

A venture involving Gulf Development pcl and PTT pcl is developing the THB31 billion third-phase Laem Chabang expansion to increase container-handling capacity. The project is part of the government’s effort to upgrade transport infrastructure in the Eastern Economic Corridor.

See also: This oil tanker tycoon's WhatsApp messages drive big market moves

A fourth phase would help accommodate longer-term growth in cargo volumes and investment in Thailand’s eastern provinces, Decha said. The authority will assess future demand before determining the project’s final scope, investment requirements and development model.

Thailand has experienced a surge in investment commitments in recent years, particularly in data centres, electronics and electric vehicle manufacturing as well as in other advanced industries. The nation’s expanding manufacturing capacity is expected to generate additional imports of machinery and raw materials while supporting future exports, adding further pressure on the country’s logistics infrastructure, according to Decha.

title: Gold climbs back from one-year low as dip buyers arrest slide
article:
(Nov 2): Gold rose as lower oil prices offered some respite from inflationary pressures and dip buyers were drawn by the metal’s slide Friday to the lowest in a year.

Bullion gained as much as 1.1% to near US$3,915 an ounce, clawing back some losses after a 3.7% slump in the previous session that rounded off the worst October for the metal since 2008. Oil dropped after Axios reported that US President Donald Trump wants to give diplomacy more time before deciding whether to resume strikes on Iran following Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Still, bullion remains vulnerable to any escalation in fighting in the Middle East. Trump has previously threatened to resume strikes on Iran after the midterms while Tehran threatened wider retaliation and several Persian Gulf states expressed concerns that another attack could unleash an even more destructive war across the region.

A global rout in technology stocks is also adding pressure to precious metals with the latest retreat from the artificial intelligence trade on Friday prompting investors to liquidate bullion to meet losses elsewhere. That selloff eased in Asian hours as regional shares fell less than their Wall Street peers and US equity futures turned higher.

Gold was finding some immediate support from long-term investors who see the current price as cheap, said Justin Lin, a strategist at Global X ETFs. “We are likely to see some dip buying in the Asian session today as investors, and possibly central banks, cautiously add to positions,” he said. “But gold is undoubtedly sitting at precarious levels.”

The metal’s drop below US$4,000 an ounce is testing the resolve of some investors, with most of the nearly 150 tonnes added to gold-backed exchange-traded fund holdings since mid-July now loss-making. That buildup in ETFs is “at risk of moving underwater as prices approach 15% to 20% below their recent peaks,” Lin said.

For now, liquidity concerns and technical selling were overshadowing the metal’s longer-term investment appeal, Ole Sloth Hansen, head of commodity strategy at Saxo Bank AS, wrote in a note. Friday’s close below the key technical level of US$3,886 an ounce “leaves gold vulnerable to additional downside pressure", he said, adding that a recovery to above US$4,000 would be needed to restore “a more neutral short-term outlook".

Spot gold climbed 0.7% to US$3,903.15 an ounce at 11.34am in Singapore. Silver gained 1.8% to US$49.98 an ounce, having dropped nearly 6% on Friday. Platinum and palladium were little changed after big declines in the previous session. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index, a gauge of the US currency, was 0.1% higher.

title: Brookfield taps KB Kookmin Bank to lead Korea’s first GPU loan at US$8 bil
article:
(Nov 2): Global investment firm Brookfield has tapped KB Kookmin Bank to be lead arranger for South Korea’s largest-ever syndicated loan that will help finance the purchase of AI chips to be used by domestic tech giant Naver Corp.

The proceeds from the financing will be used to procure AI computing infrastructure, including graphic processing units (GPU), KB said in a statement Sunday. The 10.7 trillion won (US$8 billion) loan is part of a larger package worth 12.6 trillion won, according to the bank.

The deal marks South Korea’s first sizable GPU financing and the AI chips will be leased to Naver Cloud on a long-term basis, according to the bank. Banks and private credit funds in Asia are expanding AI financing to cover not just the construction of data centres but also the hardware that powers them, such as chips.

A special purpose company established by Brookfield will procure the AI infrastructure. Other major Korean financial institutions are also participating in the deal, according to KB.

title: ACCA urges deeper CFO involvement in sustainability to enhance business resilience
article:
A new report by the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) recommends that CFOs and the finance functions of entities in the Asia Pacific should step up their involvement in sustainability reporting as sustainability is key to building business resilience.

The ACCA’s Asia Pacific builds a sustainable future report revealed that sustainability disclosure is still widely treated as a compliance exercise, with finance functions not yet translating sustainability information into risks, opportunities and business value.

The study’s insights are based on desktop research, past ACCA research, interviews, and roundtable discussions with 44 finance and accountancy professionals from across the world as well as experts on various subjects including decarbonisation, energy transition, nature, business, human rights and artificial intelligence.

The study’s interviewees and roundtable participants generally viewed alignment with the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) Standards positively as they reduce fragmentation and give companies a recognised basis for reporting.

Those who were early adopters of sustainability reporting before it was made mandatory found that their organisations had evolved from a compliance-focused mindset to leveraging sustainability-related information to make decisions in strategy and risk management deliberations, capital expenditure allocation in budgets, and risk registers, valuation, and investment decisions. These organisations made earlier investments in information architecture, established governance mechanisms, and raised board awareness.

However, several participants from Australia and ASEAN were concerned that companies with far less sustainability reporting experience were taking a more compliance-focused approach and mindset, mainly limiting disclosures to the ‘minimum viable’ level needed to avoid regulatory scrutiny. The participants stressed that sustainability-related information should be treated as core to improving business resilience and not merely as a disclosure exercise.

See also: GE Vernova exploring other tenders with Seatrium; says partnership will ‘continue for many years to come’

“Climate reporting therefore needs to be reframed as a question of business resilience, future cash flows, and balance sheet viability — not as environmental advocacy or a standalone disclosure exercise,” suggested a participant.

In addition, findings from interviews and roundtable point to limited knowledge and involvement of finance teams over sustainability in general, and reporting in particular. Cooperation between finance and sustainability teams was also perceived as weak.

"These CFOs are not seeing sustainability as a strategic business driver," said a roundtable participant. "Disappointingly, they see it as another thing to do and very much want to do the 'minimum viable compliance'."

See also: Singapore allocates $100 million to subsidise up to 75% of business-led R&D in decarbonisation

“CFOs are uncomfortable with climate scenarios because they cannot be validated with the certainty expected in conventional financial reporting,” adds another interviewee. “They may fear what the analysis will reveal about business viability, particularly under severe warming scenarios and going concern assessments.”

Addressing these concerns, ACCA suggests that boards have to assign accountability for the quality of sustainability-related financial disclosures, and how responsibility is shared across finance, sustainability, risk, and business functions.

It recommends organisations to implement a “sufficiently detailed” responsibility assignment matrix (or RACI Chart) that can improve communication and clarify responsibilities across the organisation, including how oversight is exercised when responsibilities are delegated.

ACCA Asia Pacific senior policy consultant Sharath Martin says: “This isn’t about disclosures per se, this is about making businesses more resilient.”

Using decarbonisation as an example, he adds that decarbonisation also protects businesses and economies from fossil fuel price volatility, rising costs and supply shocks. “What’s left is a capability and ownership gap, and it won’t close with time,” remarks Martin. “It closes through deliberate reframing, and CFOs are ideally placed to lead that.”

As financial and sustainability information are interconnected, professional accountants have the transferable skills and experience to ensure better connectivity in reporting, while being bound by the International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants (IESBA)’s ethical principles, notes ACCA.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The study also found that progress towards adoption and implementation of ISSB Standards in Asia Pacific is continuing despite geopolitical instability that’s severely testing business resilience in the region.

In particular, the region is leading the world in adopting global sustainability reporting standards. More than 80% of ASEAN economies by GDP have adopted or plan to adopt standards issued by the ISSB. Including the Chinese mainland, economies in the Asia Pacific region that have mandatorily or voluntarily adopted ISSB Standards represent close to US$60 ($77) trillion in GDP, approximately 47% of global GDP.

At a micro-level, the study discovered that organisation size is not necessarily a determinant of reporting maturity. ACCA found that smaller or mid-sized export-oriented firms within global supply chains may embed sustainability requirements into strategy earlier as market access depends on decarbonisation plans or product-level carbon footprints.

Conversely, larger companies serving mainly domestic markets may face weaker immediate pressure. Reporting maturity therefore develops where external expectations create urgency and internal capability turns that urgency into strategic action.

Companies that will fall within future waves of implementation in their respective jurisdictions should start developing a plan towards ISSB Standards-related disclosures readiness now by drawing on the experiences of large listed companies, suggests ACCA.

“Disclosure for its own sake, without investing in governance, data, risk management and measurement processes, may relieve short-term reporting pressure but leave businesses less prepared for future risks, regulation or customer requests,” states ACCA.

title: Goldman hikes oil-price forecasts on ‘substantial’ supply risks
article:
(Nov 2): Goldman Sachs Group Inc raised oil-price forecasts for the year-end and 2027 on elevated risks to supplies, joining other banks in hiking their outlooks after months of war in the Middle East.

Brent is now seen at US$105 a barrel in December, up from a previous estimate of US$90, and will average US$88 next year, 10% more than seen before, analysts including Daan Struyven and Yulia Zhestkova Grigsby said in a note, which also increased forecasts for US oil marker West Texas Intermediate.

“Substantial downside supply risks are likely to sustain a large, near-term risk premium,” the analysts wrote. The markets are assigning “increasing weight to escalation after the Nov 3 US midterms and subsequent potential weakness in Mideast supply,” they added in the Nov 1 report.

Global benchmark Brent rallied 14% in October, hitting a six-month high, even as crude supplies from the Middle East rebounded close to pre-war levels. The gains came on concern that hostilities between the US and Iran may flare up again after the midterm elections, with President Donald Trump repeatedly hinting that he may resume airstrikes. For his part, Iran’s Supreme Leader has ordered his top commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation.

Intensified shipping attacks and damage to infrastructure were among factors that could trigger further price gains, the analysts said, while also highlighting risks from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. “With the timing and location of disruptions nearly impossible to predict, our base case now includes a one-million-barrel-per-day global supply disruption allowance in 2027.”

See also: US pushes for Russia to resume gas sales to Europe, WSJ reports

In recent weeks, Morgan Stanley raised its forecast for Dated Brent — a key physical price — to US$105 a barrel for the fourth quarter, while ANZ Group Holdings Ltd hiked its year-end outlook for Brent futures to the same figure. Most-active contracts last traded near US$110 after dropping in Monday’s trade.

title: Binance details US$3.6 bil in net outflows after cyber theft
article:
(Nov 2): Binance posted a net outflow of US$3.6 billion ($4.6 billion) in cryptoassets after restoring customer withdrawals on Sunday, a relatively soft blow to its overall business in the wake of the largest cyber theft in history, which has been attributed to North Korean hackers.

The world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange posted details of its withdrawals and deposits on social media, saying the flight of funds eased after an initial spike. Binance had frozen withdrawals in the immediate aftermath of last Thursday’s US$6.3 billion hack to investigate and stabilise the situation, and it also pledged to reimburse all customers in full.

Although Binance got its arms around the hack relatively quickly with the help of industry partners and the US government, the digital pilferage has raised fresh questions about the vulnerabilities for cryptocurrencies and whether anyone’s money is really safe. The next-biggest attack on Bybit in 2025 was just a fraction of the latest heist.

Yet many experts were complimentary of Binance’s response to the incident, including the speed with which it reacted, the frequent updates it posted publicly to reassure customers and the idea that the platform is using its own profits for reimbursement.

It’s also hard to stop doing business with an exchange of Binance’s size and scope. The company had US$171 billion in assets under management as of Oct 28, according to its Sunday X post. The next-biggest exchange, OKX, has about US$29 billion.

“We won’t pull money off,” said Vincent Liu, the chief investment officer of Kronos Research. “Binance is the platform with most liquidity. If you want to trade or hedge in crypto, you will have to be on Binance. I do expect withdrawals but I also see many will come back as liquidity recovers.”

See also: Binance in talks for Malaysian licence after five-year absence

Still, the severity of the hack and its apparent cause — an employee’s compromised laptop — rattled confidence in Binance’s existing cybersecurity protocols and sent shockwaves across the sector earlier this week.

US government entities including the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and US Secret Service have been investigating the attack, which the FBI and blockchain-analytics firms blamed on North Korea.

The market fallout appears relatively contained so far. The value of most major cryptocurrencies changed less than 1% on Sunday. Bitcoin — which accounts for about 60% of the sector’s market value — was trading around US$78,000, roughly 5% below where it was before the theft.

See also: Trump says US looking at whether Binance hack was by North Korea

“On some level, this shows how much the industry has matured,” said Haseeb Qureshi,a managing partner of venture fund Dragonfly. “We saw extraordinarily quick responses.”

Binance has rolled out the withdrawal process gradually. The first phase covered 15 tokens, including ether and the two biggest stablecoins, Tether’s USDT and Circle Internet Group Inc’s USDC. Withdrawals on 15 blockchain networks including ethereum, BNB smart chain, XRP and base followed.

Not all of the withdrawals have been from customers because some transfers are between Binance wallets, co-chief executive officer Yi He said on X.

Binance has so far replaced about 95% of the stolen cryptocurrency using its corporate treasury, as well as emergency and insurance funds. The tokens drained in the attack were a mix of the largest cryptocurrencies across 10 blockchains, including bitcoin and ethereum.

“Our commitment remains unchanged: Binance will bear the financial impact of the stolen funds,” the company said. “These losses will not be passed on to users.”

A spate of attacks this year on crypto firms and the broader financial industry has heightened concerns that artificial intelligence (AI) is making hackers more effective — whatever venue they target. Some security experts believe North Korean hackers have incorporated AI tools into their arsenal, helping especially with reconnaissance and social engineering.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The heists have exposed serious security flaws in an industry that’s pushing into mainstream finance. Hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget in September. Hackers also stole more than US$100 million in bitcoin from wallets secured by Coinkite Inc devices, while tampering involving Ledger devices led to millions of dollars in losses.

Other recent cyberattacks have hit prediction market Polymarket, South Korean financial firms Mirae Asset Global Investments and Daishin Securities, as well as Japanese currency trading platform GMO Internet Group Inc.

Quantitative firm SQS Trading had about a quarter of its trading capital on Binance, and planned to cut that by roughly a third, founder Eli Williams said in an interview. That change won’t flatten its positions or reduce usage of the exchange as a venue for hedging, he said.

“It’s hard to forecast what the net impact will be at this point,” Williams said, “but we will be monitoring capital outflows and volume impact relative to other major venues.”

Others are holding off on changes altogether, however. Justin d’Anethan, the head of research at private markets advisory firm Arctic Digital, said he’s not fazed by the latest hack.

“When something seems fishy, it’s good to act fast, but when something catastrophic happens, it’s better to hold off doing anything,” he said. “I haven’t and wouldn’t move away from Binance.”

title: US pushes for Russia to resume gas sales to Europe, WSJ reports
article:
(Nov 2): US officials are promoting a plan for Russia to resume sales of natural gas to Europe via pipelines running through Ukraine, the Wall Street Journal reported.

The idea was promoted by US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff during trips to Moscow and Kyiv in September, and would involve selling Russian gas via a US intermediary to avoid European restrictions, the newspaper reported, citing unnamed US, European and Ukrainian officials.

The proposal was put on the back burner last month after Ukraine unilaterally stopped striking Russian refineries under pressure from US President Donald Trump, according to the WSJ. However, Kyiv has since resumed its attacks.

The US-Ukraine relationship reached a nadir last month after Trump struck a deal with President Vladimir Putin under which Washington would refrain from tightening sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow supplying limited volumes of diesel to the global market to curb rising prices.

The push from the White House comes as the European Union is set to phase out imports of Russian gas next year, which will finally sever ties between the bloc and its once-primary energy supplier. European gas prices are at their highest in almost four years, driven in part by the conflict in the Middle East, which has taken nearly a fifth of global LNG exports off the market.

Pipelines running through Ukraine are intact and gas flows could resume quickly if the US plan becomes reality. Russian exports to Europe via Ukraine were halted when a transit agreement between the two countries expired at the end of 2024, and Kyiv refused to renew it.

See also: Oil falls as report says Trump to give Iran diplomacy more time

title: Oil falls as report says Trump to give Iran diplomacy more time
article:
(Nov 2): Oil dropped on Monday after a report said US President Donald Trump wants to give diplomacy more time before deciding whether to resume strikes on Iran following Tuesday’s midterm elections.

Brent slipped towards US$111 a barrel after jumping more than 2% last Friday, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was near US$102. Trump told Benjamin Netanyahu of his preference for diplomacy in a phone call, a strategy that concerned the Israeli prime minister, Axios reported, citing people they didn’t name. The two countries started the war in late February with joint attacks on Iran.

On Saturday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said no decision had been made on fresh strikes and that Trump prefers a diplomatic resolution. The push for talks tempered concerns about renewed hostilities even as attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz continued.

The global benchmark rallied in October, hitting a six-month high despite a revival of crude flows through Hormuz. While Trump said last week that peace talks were underway, he has repeatedly threatened to resume strikes on Iran after the midterms. Last Thursday, a top commander briefed the US president on military options, The Wall Street Journal reported.

“This is a temporary pullback” in prices, said Florence Schmit, a senior energy strategist at Rabobank. Current rhetoric suggests further escalation in the Middle East is possible and could drive oil higher, she added.

Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered his top military commanders to prepare for renewed confrontation with the US and Israel, even as his foreign minister signalled progress in diplomatic talks. An Iranian delegation was in Qatar for discussions with mediators on Saturday.

See also: Big Oil scores US$56 bil windfall on war-driven refining spike

On Sunday, UK Maritime Trade Operations said it received a report that a ship had been struck by a projectile in Hormuz, following an attack on a liquefied natural gas tanker last Friday. UKMTO also reported a vessel was struck east of Ras Al Khafji, Saudi Arabia, deep inside the Persian Gulf.

While crude exports from the Persian Gulf are near prewar levels, oil-product shipments remain constrained. The Middle East conflict, along with escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian refiners, has helped drive fuel prices higher. Diesel prices have surged in the US and Europe.

Against that backdrop, Goldman Sachs Group Inc raised its Brent forecast to US$105 a barrel for December and an average of US$88 next year, citing heightened geopolitical supply risks. “The Mideast and Russia-Ukraine conflicts, alongside broader geopolitical fragmentation, create high disruption risk,” analysts including Daan Struyven and Yulia Grigsby wrote in note.

See also: Oil surges on signs US may resume military strikes against Iran

Separately, Opec+ agreed over the weekend to keep output quotas unchanged in December after unwinding the last of its voluntary cuts in September. The move is largely symbolic, given that hostilities in the Middle East, including in the Red Sea, continue to threaten exports and production facilities.

title: Stock sell-off eases in Asian trade as oil declines
article:
(Nov 2): A sell-off in stocks eased during early Monday trading as Asian equities fell less than their Wall Street peers and US equity futures turned higher. Oil declined.

Benchmark indices in Japan and Australia both fell, while those in South Korea and Hong Kong gained, leaving the MSCI Asia-Pacific Index down by 0.4%. This followed a Friday session where the Nasdaq 100 Index tumbled 3.5%, its worst day since June, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index slumped 7.2%. Futures on the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both climbed at least 0.4% on Monday, pointing to a recovery when US cash markets reopen.

Elsewhere, Brent crude fell 1.5% to about US$111.71 a barrel following reports that US President Donald Trump wants to give diplomacy more time before deciding whether to resume strikes on Iran following Tuesday’s midterm elections. Gold climbed 0.9% to around US$3,910 an ounce after falling to its lowest close in more than a year last Friday. Bitcoin climbed for a third day after sinking last week when Binance Holdings revealed a record hack that rattled the crypto industry.

China’s financial regulators will hold a meeting with banks and securities firms on Monday to discuss measures to support the capital market, signaling authorities’ renewed effort to halt the slump in Chinese stocks.

Last week’s sell-off in tech shares indicates investors are showing less tolerance for tech companies whose core businesses are slowing as artificial intelligence (AI) spending surges. Results from Alphabet Inc and Amazon.com Inc fuelled concerns that AI is eroding the businesses financing those investments. Traders are bracing for more volatility, with the US midterm elections this week and Nvidia Corp earnings later in November.

See also: Stocks slump as Wall Street gets AI wake-up call

“The revelation that these hyperscalers are seeing a slowdown in their core businesses means that the big payoff that everyone has been saying will come eventually is getting pushed even further down the road,” said Matt Maley at Miller Tabak.

All three major Chinese financial regulators, including the People’s Bank of China, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission, will hold meetings with major banks to study optimising lending programmes to support stock buy-backs, Chinese media Cailian reported on Sunday.

Binance recorded a net outflow of US$3.6 billion ($4.6 billion) in crypto assets after restoring customer withdrawals on Sunday. The world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange said the flight of funds eased after an initial spike. Binance had frozen withdrawals following last Thursday’s US$6.3 billion hack while it investigated and stabilised the platform, and pledged to reimburse customers in full.

See also: At the crossroads and in the crosshairs

The dollar was mixed against its Group-of-10 peers on Monday, while US Treasuries edged lower as risks of deepening conflict in the Middle East fanned inflation concerns.

“Markets are placing significant weight on their expectations that US‑Iran fighting will escalate after the US midterm elections on Nov 3 ,” Vivek Dhar, a strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, wrote in a note. “These concerns are justifiable given both the US and Iran believe they have the upper hand in the Middle East.”

Last Friday’s US stock slump delivered a long-awaited jolt of volatility after disappointing earnings from technology giants intensified concerns about the durability of the AI-driven rally. The Cboe Volatility Index touched its highest intraday level since April, while demand for puts protecting against further losses surged and correlations among stocks climbed, signs of mounting stress. Still, those measures remain well below levels reached in March after the US and Israel attacked Iran.

The pullback is also prompting some investors to look for buying opportunities. Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson said he sees several “clearing events” ahead that could temporarily push stocks lower and create an opportunity for investors to add exposure.

“This looks more like a bullish rotation with a derating at its core than the beginning of a broad market deterioration,” said Florian Ielpo, the head of macro research at Lombard Odier Investment Management.

title: Singapore’s STTGDC eyes US$2.4 bil loan, adds to AI debt binge — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 2): Singapore-based data centre operator STT GDC Pte Ltd (STTGDC) is in talks with banks for a $3.1 billion syndicated loan, according to people familiar with the matter, as the AI boom continues to fuel demand for debt among companies building the infrastructure.

Banks working on the planned borrowing as global coordinators, mandated lead arrangers and bookrunners include Standard Chartered plc, United Overseas Bank Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and DBS Bank Ltd, said the people, asking not to be identified discussing private details.

The three-year borrowing, which pays an interest margin of 165 basis points over the benchmark Singapore Overnight Rate Average, comes with an extension option of up to two years, the people said. Proceeds will be used as financing for STTGDC’s assets, they said.

Representatives from STTGDC, StanChart, DBS, KKR and UOB declined to comment, while Singtel and OCBC didn’t respond to a request for comment.

A group led by KKR & Co and Singapore Telecommunications Ltd completed its acquisition of STTGDC in September, after earlier agreeing to buy the data centre company for $6.6 billion. DBS, OCBC and UOB earlier participated in a $5 billion sustainability-linked loan for the purchase.

STTGDC’s deal adds to a wave of debt financing driven by the AI boom that’s also raised worries among investors with the binge pushing up bond yields, increasing scrutiny of what many see as lofty valuations of AI-linked companies.

See also: OpenAI funding target cut by US$10 bil as AI slumps — report

Globally, the AI borrowing binge has flooded markets with more than US$650 billion of debt since the start of 2025, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Moody’s Ratings expects at least US$3 trillion of data centre-related investments over the next five years.

Established in 2014, STTGDC is one of Asia’s largest data centre operators with facilities across 12 countries including India, South Korea, Japan and Malaysia, as well as the UK, Germany and Italy, according to its website.

title: PBOC conducts overnight reverse repo as policy anchor shifts
article:
(Nov 2): China’s central bank launched daily overnight reverse repurchase operations on Monday, kicking off a revamped liquidity framework that establishes the short-term tool as its primary policy anchor.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) conducted 541 billion yuan (US$81.3 billion) overnight reverse repurchases on Monday at 1.25%. After accounting for maturing reverse repos, it resulted in a net withdrawal of 515 billion yuan from the banking system, according to Bloomberg calculations.

This marks the first regular session since the PBOC unveiled the overhaul on Friday, formalising a shift away from the seven-day reverse repo rate as its primary policy anchor. Other tools that used to be based on the seven-day benchmark will be linked to the overnight rate going forward, the PBOC had said.

title: Hong Kong plans rules for insurers’ hot new growth market
article:
(Nov 2): Hong Kong is considering new rules for so-called asset-intensive reinsurance, offering clarity to firms in one of the hottest segments of the insurance market, according to people familiar with the matter.

The Hong Kong Insurance Authority has in recent months sought industry feedback on changes to its rules, including additions that for the first time specifically target asset-intensive reinsurance, the people said. The reinsurance market has come into the spotlight around the world in recent years, as firms like KKR & Co and Apollo Global Management Inc closed deals worth billions of dollars.

Asset-intensive reinsurance offers a way for insurers to juice their returns, but it also adds risks. At the most basic level, insurers shift responsibility for managing a pool of assets and liabilities to a third party, which can invest the money elsewhere to boost returns. Reinsurers have become an important source of demand for private credit, a market that has caused jitters after a yearslong boom.

Under Hong Kong’s proposed rules, insurers would either just notify the regulator or seek approval depending on the scenario. For example, insurers entering into asset-intensive reinsurance contracts with third parties need only inform the regulator — rather than get explicit approval — when the reinsurer exceeds a certain credit rating threshold, and when the firm’s overall reinsured assets aren’t material compared with their long-term liabilities. Deals that require approval will be assessed on factors including credit rating, collateral and legal enforceability, the people said.

Hong Kong’s Insurance Authority said in response to inquiries from Bloomberg News that the consultation has ended and it is reviewing the feedback. The revised guideline is expected to take effect in 2027, the regulator said.

Resolution Life, a reinsurer owned by Japan’s Nippon Life Insurance Co, said earlier this year that it had closed two reinsurance transactions in Hong Kong. HSBC Holdings Plc’s life insurance arm and Hang Seng Life Ltd were on the other side of the deals, two of the people said. Each did a US$1 billion deal with the reinsurer, one of the people said.

See also: Billionaire Friedland to build major US-backed rare earths mine

Last month, Pacific Life Re announced that it had done its first asset-intensive reinsurance deal in Hong Kong. The ceding insurer was FWD Group, one of the people said. Hong Kong insurers have used asset-intensive reinsurance to cede between US$10 billion and US$20 billion of liabilities to international reinsurance markets over the past five to seven years, according to estimates by consultancy Aon. The search for yield, greater access to private markets and regulatory changes have supported this demand, said Helbert Tsang, capital solutions leader for Asia life reinsurance at the firm.

Representatives for Resolution Life, Pacific Life Re and FWD declined to comment. HSBC and Hang Seng didn’t respond to requests for comment.

Last year, Japan’s financial regulator surveyed life insurers to examine risks tied to their growing practice of transferring policy liabilities to reinsurers backed by global investment firms, people familiar with the matter said at the time.

See also: SNB reports nine-month profit on foreign currencies and gold

Globally, the International Association of Insurance Supervisors has pointed to risks stemming from structural changes in the life insurance industry, including an increase in cross-border asset-intensive reinsurance transactions.

title: Billionaire Friedland to build major US-backed rare earths mine
article:
(Nov 2): An Australian miner led by billionaire Robert Friedland and backed by the US government has given the go-ahead for a major rare earths project.

Sunrise Energy Metals Ltd will develop the Syerston scandium mine and refinery in New South Wales with a goal to start production in 2028, it said in a statement Monday. The rare earth element is critical to defence, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence infrastructure and wireless spectrum technologies, and most supply currently comes from China.

“Since the imposition of Chinese critical minerals export controls in 2025, scandium supply to key western markets has all but ceased,” Sunrise said in the statement. “Supply risks associated with Chinese scandium supply reinforces the strategic importance of developing diversified sources of primary scandium production.”

The US and other major economies are seeking to secure supplies of critical minerals, essential to a range of advanced technologies, as they try to reduce their reliance on China’s dominant position across global supply chains. Sunrise has secured as much as US$400 million in long-term debt funding from the US Department of Defense.

The Syerston project hosts one of the world’s largest and highest-grade mineable scandium deposits, according to Melbourne-based Sunrise. The company plans initial production of 60 tonnes per year, an amount that could eventually triple.

title: LBD Engineering GM charged with operating dormitory without licence, to step down as subsidiary Metrocon's chairman
article:
Alvin Lim Yee Hong, non-executive and non-independent chairman of Metrocon Holdings, has resigned after he was charged with operating a workers' dormitory without a licence.

The charge relates to a dormitory operated by Lim via another entity LBD Engineering, where he is the general manager.

LBD Engineering is the controlling shareholder of Metrocon, with a stake of around 60%.

Lim, 35, had appeared in court on Oct 29. He plans to contest the charges but in the meantime, will step down from Metrocon, so as to focus on contesting the charge.

According to the Ministry of Manpower, LBD's premise at 58A Sungei Kadut Loop had been partially converted into a dormitory with capacity for 300 workers. Between last July and January, the dormitory housed 173 workers from four companies.

MOM says that operating a foreign employee dormitory without a valid licence is a serious offence which carries a fine of up to $500,000, imprisonment of up to two years or both.

See also: Mi Material’s stabilisation manager announces cessation of price stabilisation action; share price down more than 14%

In its separate announcement, Metrocon says that it was informed on this matter by Lim on Oct 29. According to Lim, LBD received an email from MOM on Jan 7 on the matter and was told to vacate the premise and did so accordingly.

According to Metrocon, the email correspondence between MOM and LBD in January did not indicate that either LBD or Lim was under investigation.

Lim was then called for an interview that took place on Oct 2 and he was then released on bail.

See also: Aztech rejects US$19.4 mil claim of damages from customer; mulls counter claim

Metrocon says neither the board nor the sponsor RHT Capital were informed by Lim, as he did not consider the interview with MOM falling under disclosure obligations. Neither did one

Charlotte Tay Tingyin, a non-executive and non-independent director of Metrocon, who was a director of LBD between Dec 17 2025 and Feb 13.

Metrocon, which was listed just in September after the RTO of Hatten Land, says that it is not a party to this case.

Lim's next court hearing is scheduled on Dec 13.

According to Metrocon, Lim wants to be considered for re-appointment to the board after the conclusion of the proceedings, subject to the nominating committee's assessment and regulatory approval.

Metrocon says it does not expect the charge on Lim to have any material impact on its operations or financial performance for the financial year ending 31 December 2026.

title: Karen Lee steps down as CEO of Alpha Integrated REIT; CFO steps up as CEO-Designate
article:
Alpha Integrated REIT (AI-REIT) announced that Karen Lee has stepped down as CEO of the manager with effect from Nov 2 to pursue other professional interests.

At the same time, current CFO, Goo Li Ling, has been appointed as CEO-Designate with effect from the same day.

The manager adds that Lee will remain employed until March 31, 2027 and will be available to assist the board and the CEO-Designate, with the handover of her responsibilities to ensure an orderly transition.

“The board wishes to thank Lee for her leadership, commitment and contributions during this important period in AI-REIT’s development, which has laid the foundation for the REIT’s next phase of growth,” reads the announcement.

Meanwhile, Goo will assume the office of CEO on a date to be determined by the board following receipt of the approval of the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) for her appointment, for which the manager will apply, and subject to any conditions of that approval.

Units in AI-REIT closed unchanged at 47.5 cents on Oct 30.

title: Keppel extends lease of AD110 rig by five years for US$51 mil
article:
Keppel has won a US$51 million extension lease from Arabian Drilling Company to lease one of its rigs for another five years.

The charter, won via Keppel unit RigCo is for the AD110 rig now already used in Saudi Arabia by ADC's own customer.

The AD110 rig is one of the six operational rigs identified under Keppel’s approximately $3.7 billion1 programme announced in July to progressively monetise up to 10 legacy rigs through Keppel Offshore Fund (KOF).

Under the programme, the six operational rigs are expected to be divested to KOF in 2026, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions.

The programme is designed to advance the monetisation of legacy assets while increasing Keppel’s funds under management and generating recurring asset management income.

Keppel says the charter extension reflects continuing demand for modern, high-specification jackup rigs in key offshore markets.

See also: Keppel gives Seatrium contract worth 'over' $500 mil to complete four legacy rigs

The AD110 rig was among the rigs deployed to Saudi Arabia under bareboat charter arrangements secured in 2022.

Since then, utilisation and day rates for jackup rigs have continued to remain solid amid growing preference for modern drilling units with extremely limited additional supply under construction.

"We are actively pursuing further charter contracts and renewals across our rig portfolio to strengthen contracted cash flows and enhance asset value ahead of monetisation. The transaction also reflects improving sentiment in the offshore drilling market and sustained demand for modern jackup rigs from leading operators in the Middle East," says Keppel.

Keppel shares closed at $10.09 on Oct 30, down 1.46%.

title: Trump says US-Canada trade deal is close after talks with Carney
article:
(Nov 2) : President Donald Trump said a US-Canada trade deal is “very close” after talks with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who said both sides would work on a “mutually beneficial” outcome in the weeks ahead.

“We have the concept of a very good deal with Canada,” Trump told reporters, repeating his contention that the US has been “losing money for many years” in trade with its northern neighbor.

With Republican control of Congress at risk in US midterm elections on Tuesday, Trump and Carney offered the most upbeat outlook on trade talks since they collapsed acrimoniously in August.

Carney, in a social post earlier Sunday, said he spoke with Trump, building on “recent constructive discussions” on the outlines of a deal that would create jobs, boost affordability for families and “fully respect Canada’s languages, culture and sovereignty.”

“Our teams will now be working in the coming weeks to deliver that outcome,” Carney said.

Trump’s tariff policies have spurred Carney to reduce Canadian dependence on trade with the US. Last week, he hosted top European Union officials in Montreal as part of the effort to deepen ties with non-US trade partners.

See also: Asian stocks to fall as tech rout fuels AI fears

After the EU meeting, Carney hinted in a Politico interview that the outcome of the US midterms wouldn’t have much of an impact on shifting Trump’s policy stance. Canada won’t rush into a trade agreement with the US if the terms aren’t in Canada’s best interest, he said.

“I spoke with the prime minister the other day,” Trump said Sunday, referring to Carney. “I spoke to him again yesterday, and we have the concept of a deal that’s going to be great for our farmers, great for our country, and it will be fine for Canada.”

US-Canada trade talks collapsed in August when Carney’s envoy walked away from the deal, in part over a dispute about whether to extend proposed US tariff relief to medium and heavy-duty vehicles that Canada was seeking.

See also: Oil declines as traders parse signs of fresh diplomacy on Iran

Canada also accused the US of seeking to curtail the use of French, one of Canada’s two official languages. The US has denied that.
